c1g-overshot-driveway-reverse.distinctiveMechanism: The lead car ahead suddenly slows and reverses in the ego lane toward the missed driveway.
c1g-overshot-driveway-reverse.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for reversing, overshooting a driveway, or passing within a specified distance; DECELERATES_HARD is the closest checkable proxy for the sudden reversal, and TURNS supports the driveway manoeuvre.
c1g-overshot-driveway-reverse.brief: The lead car overshoots a driveway and suddenly reverses in the ego lane to reach it, forcing the ego to brake hard or pass within a couple of metres.

c10g-detached-wheel.distinctiveMechanism: A detached wheel rolls from outside the ego's travelled corridor into the ego path.
c10g-detached-wheel.notes: The vocabulary cannot directly express detachment from the car, rolling, the centreline, the hidden pothole, or hard braking by the ego; ONCOMING(car) captures the supporting oncoming-car detail.
c10g-detached-wheel.brief: A wheel detaches from an oncoming car after it strikes a hidden pothole and rolls across the centreline into the ego lane, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c11g-wide-bay-turn.distinctiveMechanism: The pickup turns into an angled parking bay while swinging across the ego vehicle's path.
c11g-wide-bay-turn.notes: A pickup is represented by the truck class. The brief explicitly requires hard braking or a close pass; the response vocabulary has no separate close-pass option, so either is the closest representation.
c11g-wide-bay-turn.brief: A pickup swings wide while turning into an angled parking bay and crosses the ego vehicle's lane, forcing hard braking or a close pass.

c12g-backward-school-gate.distinctiveMechanism: The child emerges from behind a parked SUV into the ego vehicle's path.
c12g-backward-school-gate.notes: SUV is represented by the available car class; the child's backward walking and the school gate are not expressible predicates.
c12g-backward-school-gate.brief: A parked SUV hides a child walking backward from a school gate until the child steps off the curb into the ego lane, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c13-officer-override.distinctiveMechanism: A temporary traffic signal or a traffic officer overrides the normal traffic control.
c13-officer-override.notes: The available predicates cannot express traffic-control authority or an override, and the brief gives an either/or alternative. PRESENT(object) or PRESENT(pedestrian) would not be sufficient because mere presence does not establish a temporary signal or an officer directing traffic.
c13-officer-override.brief: Temporary signals or an officer override the normal control.

c14-friction-patch.distinctiveMechanism: The lead vehicle loses traction on a friction patch.
c14-friction-patch.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for loss of traction or for a friction patch; 'vehicle' is normalized to car, and the patch itself is scenery rather than a required actor.
c14-friction-patch.brief: A vehicle ahead loses traction on a friction patch.

c15-protest.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian unexpectedly moves from outside into the ego vehicle's travelled corridor.
c15-protest.notes: The wording implies an unexpected encroachment into the carriageway, but does not require the ego vehicle to brake or swerve.

c2g-bicycle-avoids-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: The cyclist shifts from outside the ego corridor into the ego path.
c2g-bicycle-avoids-pedestrian.notes: The vocabulary does not encode the cyclist's edge-line position, avoidance motive, or causal forcing of the ego response; these are represented by cyclist path entry and the required ego braking response.
c2g-bicycle-avoids-pedestrian.brief: A bicycle travelling along the road edge shifts across the edge line into the ego lane to avoid a pedestrian at the kerb, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c3g-right-turn-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian steps from outside the ego's travelled corridor into it, creating an immediate conflict that requires hard braking.
c3g-right-turn-pedestrian.notes: The pedestrian's adult status, the green signal, the ego's right turn, the exit-crossing label, and the ego's hard-braking intensity are not separately expressible as predicates; the required response is captured by egoResponse.
c3g-right-turn-pedestrian.brief: As the ego turns right through a green signal, an adult pedestrian steps into the exit crossing and forces the ego to brake hard.

c4-exit-cut.distinctiveMechanism: A circulating car crosses the ego vehicle's exit path.
c4-exit-cut.notes: The brief says vehicle but does not specify a more specific class; car is used as the generic vehicle realization.
c4-exit-cut.brief: A circulating vehicle cuts across the ego exit path.

c5g-shoulder-drift.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian shifts from the road edge into the ego vehicle's travelled corridor as the ego overtakes.
c5g-shoulder-drift.notes: Hard braking and a close pass are required by the wording but are not directly representable by the supplied predicates; egoResponse captures the braking requirement.
c5g-shoulder-drift.brief: An adult walking along the road edge in the ego vehicle's direction suddenly shifts into the live lane as the ego overtakes, forcing hard braking and a close pass.

c6g-cyclist-hidden-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: The cyclist suddenly swerves into the ego vehicle's path.
c6g-cyclist-hidden-pedestrian.notes: The vocabulary cannot directly encode the pedestrian stepping into the cyclist's path or carrying a box; OCCLUDED_BY(pedestrian, van) captures the van-obscured emergence, while ENTERS_EGO_PATH(cyclist) captures the cyclist's swerve into the ego lane.
c6g-cyclist-hidden-pedestrian.brief: A pedestrian carrying a large box steps out from behind a parked van into a cyclist's path, causing the cyclist to swerve suddenly into the ego lane and forcing hard braking.

c7g-hidden-car-door.distinctiveMechanism: A parked car's door opens into the ego vehicle's path while the car is temporarily hidden by the adjacent truck.
c7g-hidden-car-door.notes: The vocabulary cannot represent a door separately, adjacency, or the truck's motion; ENTERS_EGO_PATH(car) is used to represent the door encroachment.
c7g-hidden-car-door.brief: A moving box truck in the adjacent lane hides a parked car's door opening into the ego vehicle's path until the ego vehicle is alongside, forcing an immediate swerve or hard brake.

c8-shifted-alignment.distinctiveMechanism: The ego laterally steers around a work-zone obstruction ahead.
c8-shifted-alignment.notes: The work zone is represented as an object; no listed predicate directly describes roadway alignment shifts or ego steering.
c8-shifted-alignment.brief: A work zone shifts the alignment laterally and the ego steers around it.

c9g-falling-tree-branch.distinctiveMechanism: A bus pulls a roadside branch, represented as an object, down into the ego vehicle's path ahead of it.
c9g-falling-tree-branch.notes: The vocabulary cannot express the bus-branch causal interaction, the branch's low height, or the close-pass response; object represents the branch.
c9g-falling-tree-branch.brief: A tall bus catches a low roadside tree branch and pulls it down into the ego lane just ahead of the ego vehicle, forcing hard braking or a close pass.

c1-ccrm.distinctiveMechanism: The ego closes on a slower-moving car ahead in the same travel corridor.
c1-ccrm.notes: The vocabulary cannot directly encode relative speed or closing speed; car is used as the closest available class for the generic lead vehicle.
c1-ccrm.brief: A slower lead vehicle is encountered at closing speed (Euro NCAP CCRm).

c10g-left-turn-no-yield.distinctiveMechanism: An oncoming car crosses the ego vehicle's path while turning left.
c10g-left-turn-no-yield.notes: SUV is mapped to the available car class. The vocabulary has no explicit predicate for failing to yield, being at an unsignalised junction, or forcing the ego to brake; the required ego response is therefore given separately.
c10g-left-turn-no-yield.brief: An oncoming SUV begins a left turn across the ego's lane at an unsignalised junction without yielding, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c11g-wrong-way-aisle.distinctiveMechanism: A motorcycle pulls into the ego's travel corridor and proceeds against the ego's direction toward it.
c11g-wrong-way-aisle.notes: The brief explicitly mentions braking and shifting aside, but the response vocabulary cannot require both; "either" represents the required evasive response category.
c11g-wrong-way-aisle.brief: A motorcycle exits a parking row and travels the wrong way down the marked aisle toward the ego vehicle, forcing the ego to brake and shift aside.

c12-crossing-guard.distinctiveMechanism: Pedestrians cross the ego vehicle's path after being released by a crossing guard.
c12-crossing-guard.notes: The vocabulary cannot distinguish a crossing guard from the children or represent the release action or plurality explicitly; these are abstracted as pedestrians, with at least one pedestrian crossing the ego path.
c12-crossing-guard.brief: A crossing guard releases children across the ego path.

c13-signal-outage.distinctiveMechanism: The junction's traffic signal is out of service and flashing.
c13-signal-outage.notes: The brief describes infrastructure and signal state, neither of which is representable by the supplied actor classes or predicates.
c13-signal-outage.brief: A signal outage leaves the junction flashing.

c14g-motorcycle-drain-grate.distinctiveMechanism: The motorcycle loses control and skids from near the curb into the ego vehicle's path.
c14g-motorcycle-drain-grate.notes: The grate, rider fall, and hard braking or passing are not directly expressible as actor predicates; the grate is treated as causal scenery rather than a required object.
c14g-motorcycle-drain-grate.brief: A motorcycle's front wheel drops into a longitudinal storm-drain grate near the curb, throwing the rider down as the bike skids into the ego lane and forces hard braking or a pass within a couple of metres.

c15g-red-light-runner.distinctiveMechanism: A van moves from outside into the ego vehicle's travelled corridor.
c15g-red-light-runner.notes: Signalization, the van's red signal violation, the ego's green signal, and the junction context are not expressible with the available predicates.
c15g-red-light-runner.brief: At a signalized junction, a van ignores its red signal and enters across the ego's lane just as the ego proceeds on green, forcing hard braking.

c2g-static-object-lane-shift.distinctiveMechanism: The van moves from the adjacent lane into the ego vehicle's travelled path.
c2g-static-object-lane-shift.notes: The vocabulary cannot directly encode that the object is large, static, in the van's lane, or that the van fails to yield; these details are conveyed only by the brief and the required ego response.
c2g-static-object-lane-shift.brief: A van in the adjacent lane moves around a large static object placed in its lane and enters the ego lane without yielding, requiring the ego to brake hard.

c3g-child-behind-bus.distinctiveMechanism: The pedestrian runs across the ego vehicle's turning path.
c3g-child-behind-bus.notes: The ego's left-turn manoeuvre and hard braking are captured by the scenario wording and egoResponse rather than by an available ego-specific predicate.
c3g-child-behind-bus.brief: As the ego turns left into a side road, a child pedestrian emerges from behind a bus and runs across the turning path, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c4g-central-pedestrian-intrusion.distinctiveMechanism: The pedestrian steps from outside the ego's corridor into its travelled path as the ego approaches.
c4g-central-pedestrian-intrusion.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for a central island, hard braking by the ego, or close passing distance; these are represented by the scenario wording and egoResponse where possible.
c4g-central-pedestrian-intrusion.brief: An adult pedestrian steps from the central island into the circulating lane as the ego approaches, forcing the ego to brake hard and pass close behind.

c5g-truck-screened-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian crosses into the ego path while initially hidden behind an oncoming truck.
c5g-truck-screened-pedestrian.notes: “Box truck” maps to the truck class; the required hard braking and short remaining distance are represented by egoResponse because no predicate directly encodes ego braking distance.
c5g-truck-screened-pedestrian.brief: An oncoming box truck hides an adult pedestrian crossing into the ego lane until the truck clears, leaving the ego vehicle only a short distance to brake hard.

c6g-motorcycle-cargo-spill.distinctiveMechanism: A bag dropped from the motorcycle enters the ego path.
c6g-motorcycle-cargo-spill.notes: The available predicates cannot explicitly represent the loose strap, detachment, falling, bouncing, or causal connection to the motorcycle; ENTERS_EGO_PATH(object) captures the required lane intrusion.
c6g-motorcycle-cargo-spill.brief: A motorcycle ahead loses an unsecured bag when its luggage strap comes loose, and the bag drops and bounces into the ego lane, forcing hard braking.

c7-bus-occludes-cyclist.distinctiveMechanism: A bus physically occludes a cyclist from the ego before they meet
c7-bus-occludes-cyclist.notes: The brief does not require the cyclist to move, enter the ego path, or trigger an ego response. The available predicates do not directly encode a bus that is simply stationary; MOVES_THEN_STOPS would impose the stronger requirement that it was previously moving.
c7-bus-occludes-cyclist.brief: A stopped bus hides a cyclist from the ego.

c8g-temporary-fence-collapse.distinctiveMechanism: A mesh fence panel collapses from outside the ego corridor into the ego path as the vehicle approaches
c8g-temporary-fence-collapse.notes: The vocabulary cannot explicitly encode a fence, mesh construction, sidewalk origin, collapse, or passing distance; these are represented by an object entering the ego path.
c8g-temporary-fence-collapse.brief: A temporary mesh fence panel collapses from the sidewalk into the ego lane as the vehicle approaches, forcing the ego to brake hard or pass within a couple of metres.

c9g-displaced-drain-grate.distinctiveMechanism: A storm-drain grate intrudes into the ego vehicle's path while initially concealed by a parked SUV.
c9g-displaced-drain-grate.notes: The vocabulary cannot explicitly encode that the grate is lifted diagonally, that the SUV is parked, or that the required response occurs only at close range; 'either' represents hard braking or a narrow swerve/pass.
c9g-displaced-drain-grate.brief: A storm-drain grate has lifted diagonally into the curb lane and is concealed by a parked SUV until the ego vehicle is close enough to require hard braking or a narrow pass.

c1g-bus-pulls-out.distinctiveMechanism: A stationary bus pulls out from the kerb into the ego vehicle's path.
c1g-bus-pulls-out.notes: The vocabulary does not encode failure to yield, very low speed, hard braking specifically, or passing within a couple of metres; either covers the stated braking-or-evasive response.
c1g-bus-pulls-out.brief: A bus pulls away from the kerb directly into the ego lane without yielding and continues at very low speed, forcing the ego to brake hard or pass within a couple of metres.

c10-ego-overtake.distinctiveMechanism: The ego assesses whether it can pass a vehicle ahead while an oncoming vehicle occupies the opposing approach.
c10-ego-overtake.notes: The brief does not state that the ego actually overtakes or performs any manoeuvre; 'traffic' is represented canonically as cars.
c10-ego-overtake.brief: The ego judges a gap to overtake with oncoming traffic.

c11-backing-out.distinctiveMechanism: A stationary vehicle backs out of a parking space and moves into the ego vehicle's travelled path
c11-backing-out.notes: The brief says vehicle rather than a specific available actor class; car is used as the closest generic vehicle class. The vocabulary cannot explicitly encode reversing or a parking space.
c11-backing-out.brief: A vehicle backs out of a parking space into the ego path.

c12-school-dropoff.distinctiveMechanism: Children and vehicles are present together in a school drop-off setting.
c12-school-dropoff.notes: Children map to pedestrian. The brief says vehicles generically, but no generic vehicle class is available, so no particular vehicle class is required. It does not explicitly require a pedestrian to enter or cross the ego path, or require an ego response.
c12-school-dropoff.brief: Chaotic school drop-off with vehicles and children.

c14g-bicycle-chain-lock.distinctiveMechanism: The cyclist slews sideways from beside the ego lane into the ego's travelled path.
c14g-bicycle-chain-lock.notes: The vocabulary cannot explicitly encode a chain jam, pedalling, or rear-wheel slewing; the required encroachment is represented by ENTERS_EGO_PATH(cyclist).
c14g-bicycle-chain-lock.brief: A cyclist's chain jams while pedalling beside the ego lane, making the rear wheel slew sideways and pushing the bicycle into the ego's path so the ego must brake hard or pass within a couple of metres.

c15-shedding-load.distinctiveMechanism: The truck ahead sheds or loses part of its load.
c15-shedding-load.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for a load detaching from a truck, so PRESENT(object) represents the shed load but cannot encode the shedding relationship itself.
c15-shedding-load.brief: A truck ahead sheds part of its load.

c2g-motorcycle-door-avoidance.distinctiveMechanism: The motorcycle swerves from beside the parked cars into the ego's path.
c2g-motorcycle-door-avoidance.notes: The vocabulary cannot represent a car door opening, parked status, filtering, or causal forcing; these are captured only indirectly by the motorcycle's entry into the ego path and the required hard-braking response.
c2g-motorcycle-door-avoidance.brief: A motorcycle filtering past the ego beside parked cars swerves back into the ego lane when a parked-car door opens, forcing the ego to brake hard.

c3-cross-traffic-violation.distinctiveMechanism: Cross traffic proceeds through its stop control and crosses into the ego vehicle's path at a junction
c3-cross-traffic-violation.notes: The brief does not specify the cross-traffic vehicle class; car is used as the closest conventional representative. The stop-control violation itself is not directly expressible in the available predicates.
c3-cross-traffic-violation.brief: Cross traffic runs the stop control into the ego path at a junction.

c4g-hidden-entry-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian emerges from behind a stopped van into the ego's entry path.
c4g-hidden-entry-pedestrian.notes: The vocabulary cannot encode the van being beside the splitter, the ego reaching the yield line, or the exact timing and severity of the ego's braking.
c4g-hidden-entry-pedestrian.brief: A van stopped beside the entry splitter hides a pedestrian who steps into the ego's entry lane as the ego reaches the yield line, forcing hard braking.

c5-reversing-ped.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian moves in the space behind the ego vehicle while that vehicle reverses.
c5-reversing-ped.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for reversing or generic walking; BEHIND_EGO assumes the reversing vehicle is the ego vehicle.
c5-reversing-ped.brief: A pedestrian walks behind a reversing vehicle.

c6g-oncoming-motorcycle-truck-overtake.distinctiveMechanism: The motorcycle encroaches into the ego vehicle's path while overtaking the truck.
c6g-oncoming-motorcycle-truck-overtake.notes: The vocabulary cannot represent overtaking, crossing the centre line, relative timing, hard braking, or the resulting survivable gap directly; ENTERS_EGO_PATH is used as the closest required representation of the centre-line encroachment.
c6g-oncoming-motorcycle-truck-overtake.brief: An oncoming motorcycle overtakes a slow-moving truck across the centre line just as the ego vehicle approaches, forcing the ego to brake hard and leave a survivable gap.

c7g-overtaking-motorcycle.distinctiveMechanism: The motorcycle emerges from behind an oncoming bus into the ego vehicle's travelled path.
c7g-overtaking-motorcycle.notes: The available predicates do not explicitly encode overtaking, crossing the centre line, or causal forcing; these are approximated by the motorcycle entering the ego path, the bus being oncoming, and the motorcycle being occluded by the bus.
c7g-overtaking-motorcycle.brief: An oncoming bus masks a motorcycle overtaking it across the centre line until the rider appears in the ego vehicle's lane, forcing hard braking.

c8g-cyclist-emerges-from-barriers.distinctiveMechanism: A cyclist emerges from behind an occluding roadside barrier into the ego vehicle's travelled path.
c8g-cyclist-emerges-from-barriers.notes: The roadside barriers are represented as an object; the available egoResponse labels cannot separately encode braking hard and steering around the cyclist, so either is the closest label.
c8g-cyclist-emerges-from-barriers.brief: A cyclist suddenly emerges from behind roadside barriers into the live lane beside the roadworks, forcing the ego to brake hard and steer around the bicycle.

c9-accident-scene.distinctiveMechanism: A physical accident-related obstruction is ahead and occupies part of the ego vehicle's lane.
c9-accident-scene.notes: The vocabulary has no predicate for lane occupancy or an accident scene; AHEAD_OF_EGO(object) is the closest available representation. No ego response is stated or required.
c9-accident-scene.brief: An accident scene partially blocks the ego lane.

c1g-hidden-pedestrian.distinctiveMechanism: A pedestrian emerges into the ego vehicle's path from between parked vehicles.
c1g-hidden-pedestrian.notes: The brief explicitly describes hard braking by the lead car, while the ego may either brake hard or pass very closely; the available predicates do not encode the couple-of-metres clearance or causal forcing.
c1g-hidden-pedestrian.brief: The lead car brakes hard when a pedestrian steps from between parked vehicles into its lane, forcing the ego to brake hard or pass within a couple of metres.

c10g-trailer-jackknife.distinctiveMechanism: The pickup's trailer jackknifes into the ego's travelled path across the centreline.
c10g-trailer-jackknife.notes: Pickup is mapped to truck and the trailer is approximated as object because trailer is not an available actor class. The cyclist need not enter the ego's path; it only needs to be present as the reason the oncoming pickup brakes.
c10g-trailer-jackknife.brief: An oncoming pickup brakes sharply for a cyclist wobbling into its lane and its small trailer jackknifes across the centreline, forcing the ego to brake hard.
